verbalization: The visible evidence suggests that Oblonganoside C may interact with Tyrosine-protein kinase Yes through a series of molecular pathways. Specifically, Oblonganoside C is predicted to target Serine/threonine-protein kinase ICK, which is a known target of Ent-Gloeosteretriol. This kinase, in turn, is predicted to target Tyrosine-protein kinase Yes, forming a direct pathway from Oblonganoside C to the kinase of interest. Similarly, Oblonganoside C is also predicted to interact with Serine/threonine-protein kinase SBK1, which is a target of Theasaponin E1, which also targets Tyrosine-protein kinase Yes. These findings collectively indicate that Oblonganoside C may exert its biological effects through a network of kinase pathways that ultimately lead to the activation of Tyrosine-protein kinase Yes. The integration of these pathways suggests a potential mechanism by which Oblonganoside C could influence cellular signaling, though the exact nature of the interaction and its functional implications remain to be fully elucidated.
